subject.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow

question: Should OpenClaw core sponsor this native encrypted folder-backed snapshot flow once the safety blockers and proof gap are resolved, or should the PR be narrowed/closed in favor of existing local export plus external backup tooling?
rationale: The branch adds new CLI commands, persisted config, encrypted backup storage, and destructive restore behavior; automation can identify defects, but maintainers must choose the supported product and upgrade contract.

options.title: Sponsor after blockers
options.body: Keep the PR open and require the remaining safety fixes, upgrade/compatibility review, and redacted real behavior proof before any merge.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Ask for a smaller PR that only hardens existing backup export/verify behavior while leaving snapshot setup/run/restore for a later design.

options.title: Close as product mismatch
options.body: Close this PR if maintainers decide folder-backed encrypted snapshots should live outside core or wait for a different backup architecture.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after blockers
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open and require the remaining safety fixes, upgrade/compatibility review, and redacted real behavior proof before any merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup docs/tests and validation refactors make him the best available owner for product-scope and proof expectations, though the original author remains important implementation context.
